searchText: Any particular reason to use 6s slot for minimal. Only rationale I find is faster for testing purpose. The downside of 6s slot is that's going to complicate production monitoring and we are advocating against it If there's no strong use case or reasoning, can we change it back to 12s? +1 ^ would like to see a minimal testnet with the same time parameters as mainnet. Curious about the testing use case for shorter slot times in minimal conifg I think a lower test block time does help to create a safety margin. Maybe we do not need 50% margin though <@476250636548308992>, I think all three fields might as well be random data. (that's how we've implemented it) basically, the objective is to _not_ form a majority https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/f2f0c038aacc75a0325f1788bcc760301b10b1d9/beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/eth1_chain.rs#L254-L275 ah k yeap that makes sense as long as each proposer has a different eth1Data we will not be able to form a majority yep! <@203220829473996800> what is a safety margin in phase 0? Meant to say that if processing is not possible within 12s - margin, then surviving during a more stressful chain load is difficult. Also remember what Jacek said during interop: running on 99% resources (any kind) will make you, as a node, fall over and get into a death spiral with the slightest spike in workload. Yes but wouldn’t that be discovered in benchmarking and tests? We have some (not much) monitoring on the block / attestation rates which are affected by a change in slot times I suppose it’s not that big of a change as long as we do cross client with mainnet slot times before launch I would suggest parametrizing slot time in your monitoring tools. It is very likely that we run testnets with even shorter slot times to induce forking and other interseting behaviors on testnets. I also expect private chains and other environments to use different slot times and being able to reuse the tooling for these will be useful how to parameterize yaml 🤣 all good, we'll figure it out
